claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Senators are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Senators take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.
claims.call: The Panthers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Senators.

claims.head: The Senators will send their checkers at Reinhart
claims.call: The Senators’ L4 (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) spends at least 54% of its 5-on-5 time against the Panthers’ first line, against about 42% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Pinto’s line (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Panthers’ first line is Verhaeghe, Reinhart and Eller.

claims.gist: At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Panthers’ first line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 37% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 4% last season.

stakes: The Panthers and the Senators go in level on 12 points, third and third in the Atlantic in the Atlantic. A win in regulation would put either one ahead of the other.

OTT.head: Leaning the Senators’ way
OTT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Ottawa has home-ice advantage. The Panthers can still swing it if they keep shots to a minimum.

FLA.head: The Panthers start a half-step behind
FLA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Ottawa has home-ice advantage. The Panthers can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Brady Tkachuk returns to Ottawa
paras: The Senators are 6-3-0. The Panthers have won three straight, the last an 8-3 rout of Seattle.

It’s strength against strength: the Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Senators are near the top at the penalty kill. At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Cats’ first line.

items.text: Brady Tkachuk faces Ottawa for the first time since leaving.
The Panthers are newly without Jacob Markström, and have been without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for several games. Akira Schmid is expected to start.
Drake Batherson has a point in five straight games against Florida, with a goal in each of the last four.
The Senators are newly without Thomas Chabot, and have been without William Eklund since Oct 8.
